This criminal appeal under Section 374(2) of the Cr.P.C. is directed against the judgment dated 30.06.2011 passed by First Additional Sessions Judge, Surajpur, District Surajpur (C.G.) in Sessions Trial No. 44/2010 whereby and whereunder, the appellant has been convicted under Section 376 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for seven years with fine of Rs.100/-, in default of payment of fine, to further undergo R. I. for 10 days.

Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that victim, who is aged about 45 years, has lodged a written complaint (Ex.P-4) before Police Station Premnagar alleging therein that on the fateful day i.e. on 29.09.2009, at about 11 pm in the night, she was sleeping in her room and her husband -Babua Ram and her father-in-law (Mousa Sasur) were sleeping in the courtyard, which is adjacent to the room, at that time, appellant unauthorisely entered in her room and committed rape on her.
It is further alleged that when the victim cried for help, then her husband and Bigam Ram came there and caught hold the appellant and tied him, which was seen by the villagers also.
It is also the case of the victim, that appellant has also assaulted her husband and her family members.
Thereafter, the matter has been reported to the police, then police came there and instead of arresting the appellant/accused, has arrested the family members of the victim.

Thereafter she lodged a writeent complaint against the appellant and on the basis of the written complaint filed by the victim, appellant has been arrested and FIR bearing Crime No. 84/2009 has been lodged against the appellant under Sections 456 & 376 of the IPC.
Thereafter, the appellant and the victim were sent for their medical examination.
Evidence of the witnesses were recorded.
Seizure has been made and spot map was prepared.

6. After completion of the usual investigation, a charge sheet was filed against the appellant for the offence punishable under Sections 450 & 376 of the IPC before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Surajpur, who has committed the case to the Court of learned Sessions Judge,
Ambikpuar and the learned Sessions Judge framed the charges against the appellant under 376 of the IPC.

sentences.text: Charge was read over and explained to the accused, who abjured his guilt.

7. In order to bring home the offence, the prosecution examined as many as 6 witnesses namely victim (PW-1), Babua Ram (PW-2), Chandrakanta {Lady constable} (PW-3), Rakesh Sahu (PW-4),
Amol Singh (PW-5) & J.L.Lakda (PW-6) and exhibited Property Seizure Memo (Ex.P-1), Mulahija Prativedan (Ex.P-2), Spot Map (Ex.P-3), Written Report (Ex.P- 4), FIR (Ex.P-5) & Crime Details (Ex.P-6).
8. Statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. in which he denied the circumstances appearing against him and stated that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
He has neither examined any witness nor exhibited any documents in support of his submission.
9. Babua Ram (PW-2), who is husband of the victim, has admitted in his cross-examination that three years ago, he had a dispute with the accused/appellant and a report was also filed in this regard.
It is also admitted by this witness that a case and counter case was filed against both the parties and they have compromised in the matter.
But he has denied the fact that aforesaid case was related with the relationship between the appellant & her wife.

Further, although, the doctor, who has medically examined the victim, has not been examined by the prosecution, but as per medical report (Ex.P-2) of the victim, no definite opinion can be given about the rape upon the victim and further opined that she is habitual to sexual intercourse, as she is married lady.

2 10.

Learned trial Court upon appreciation of oral and documentary evidence available on record, by its judgment dated 30.06.2011 has convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 376 of the IPC and sentenced him as has been stated in preceding paragraph, against which, this criminal appeal has been filed.

11. During trial the appellant was in jail since 02.10.2009 to 17.11.2009 i.e. 1 month & 15 days,
thereafter, after conviction by the trial Court he was in jail since 30.06.2011 and thereafter, the appellant has been released on bail by this Court vide order 05.08.2011 i.e. one month & 5 days,
thus, the appellant has remained in jail for about two months and twenty days.

12. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question, as the case of the prosecution is doubtful and the prosecution has not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.

He further submits that as per version of the victim, it seems that victim is a consenting party to the act of the appellant and she had established physical relation with the appellant with her own will, because it is doubtful that she was sleeping in her room and her husband were sleeping in a courtyard and distance between aforesaid two places is very short i.e. 1  meter, then if she could have raised objection to the aforesaid wrong act committed by the appellant, then her husband & other persons definitely heard her noise, thus, it is prayed the appeal may be allowed by giving benefit of doubt to the accused/appellant.
13. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State would submit that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.

It is submitted that it is well settled position of law that statement of the victim cannot be ignored, unless such evidence is rebutted through cogent evidence by the other side; but in the instant case, the appellant has not examined any witness to rebut the aforesaid allegations made against him, hence, the learned trial Court is absolutely justified in convicting and sentencing the accused/appellant by the impugned order, which does not call for any interference.
14. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the court below.

15. Now, this Court has to ascertain whether the finding recorded by the trial Court for convicting the accused / appellant under Section 376 of the IPC is legal or not and deserves to be interfered with or not.

16. To appreciate the aforesaid issue, entire evidence adduced by the prosecution is taken into consideration, especially in the rape case, statement of the victim has to be seen for the purpose of just decision of the case.

17. Victim (PW-1) has stated in her statement that on the date of incident her husband was sleeping in courtyard whereas she was sleeping in the room and door of the room was not closed, then at about 11.00 pm in the night accused/appellant came in her room and committed rape on her and when she raised alarm to rescue her, then her husband and family members woke-up, came there,
caught hold of the appellant and tied him with rope.

Further, in the cross-examination, she has specifically stated, she did not lodge the report of incident immediately in the night but when her husband and brother-in-law (Dewar) were taken into custody by the police

, then only on the next Baliram vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131268803/
3 day of the incident, she lodged report against the appellant.
She has further stated in her evidence that her husband and son committed Marpeet with appellant/accused, as he entered in the house unauthorizedly and committed rape on her.

She has denied that three years ago, her husband lodged report in the police Station with regard to illicit relation between her and the appellant and she has also denied that she has compromised the aforesaid matter.
When a specific question was asked to victim, when the accused/appellant committed rape on her, why she did not raise any objection,
then she replied that, when she smelled the alcohol, then she felt that there was someone else in place of her husband, that is why she raised an alarm.

She has further stated that her husband slept in the courtyard and she slept in the room and the courtyard and the room are adjacent to each other, there must have been a distance of about one and a half meters.

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case particularly the statement of the victim it is quite vivid that If the victim could have raised objection, then her husband definitely heard the same.

As such, it is held that the victim has sufficient opportunity to rescue her, but she did not do so, that too, her husband was sleeping in a very short distance from her in the courtyard along her Mousa Sasur.

Apart from this, the trial Court has not recorded a finding about the injuries sustained by the victim in the said incident and even the doctor, who has medically examined the victim, has not been examined by the prosecution in support of its case.
Thus, this court is of the opinion, that appellant/accused is entitled for acquittal of the alleged offence by giving benefit of doubt.
19. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
Conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court is set aside.
The appellant is acquitted of the charge under Section 376 of IPC.
The appellant is reported to be on bail.

His bail bond shall continue for a further period of six months from today in view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C.
